full_judgment: 31. It is patently clear that the appellant previously manufactured his goods (the same goods as he is now manufacturing) under the trademark 'Lucky' of which the title was assigned to him, but that trade-mark registration No.38818 is class 6 under the mark "Lucky" was removed from the Trade Marks Register by order of the High Court Division passed in Trade Mark Application No.04 of 2001. That removal was upheld by this Division on 13.07.2003. The appellant is now manufacturing and marketing the very same goods under the trademark 'Lucky Star'. The High Court Division in the impugned judgment concluded that this was in violation of sections 8 and 10 of the Trade Marks Act, 1940. In this regard reference may be made to the decision in the case of Baby food products Ltd. Aga Nawab Dowry, Dhaka v. Nabisco Biscuit and Bread Factory Ltd. 262, Tejgaon Industrial Area Dhaka and. another 30BLD(AD)25. In the cited case the respondent manufactured and marketed biscuits under the trademark "Nabisco", whereas the appellants manufactured and marketed goods imitating the trademark of the respondent and secretly filed an application for registration of the trademark consisting of a deceptively similar trademark `Nabico'. This Division held as follows: "It appears that whatever product the petitioner is producing and selling in the trade name of NABICO is likely to deceive the people at large who will presume the products to be of NABISCO being misled by the similarity in sounds and as such this is no ground to review our judgment already passed."
